title: The remote viewing photo protocol and its 35% hit rate, replicated at Edinburgh and the Rhine institute
place_text: SRI; University of Edinburgh; Rhine Research Institute, Duke, North Carolina

tellings.quote: the study of these attempts found that there was an overall hit rate of 35% a number that was found to be repeatable over and over again

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe a distant place or a hidden photo using only the mind, which was tested with photos from the 1970s to the 1990s at the Stanford Research Institute, a research lab in California. He says a review of these attempts, citing a researcher named Jessica Utts, found an overall hit rate of 35 percent, a number repeated again and again, including at the University of Edinburgh and at the Rhine Research Institute at Duke in North Carolina. If true, it would suggest the mind can pick up information beyond the ordinary senses.
